title: Make your own tree
summary: Create a tree, give it a first step, and save it.

say.never: A **tree** is one autonomous routine, saved as its own file. You'll make a new one called `MyFirstAuto`, put a **Sequence** at the top (the step that runs the others in order), and save it.
say.bit: Make a tree called `MyFirstAuto`, start it with a Sequence, save.

say.never: Click **+ New tree**, at the top of the **Trees** list on the left.
Type `MyFirstAuto` in the **Tree ID** box. Leave **A new file** picked, so it gets a file of its own. Then click **Create**.

waitFor.hint: name it MyFirstAuto and click Create.

say.never: The canvas is empty. In the **Nodes** list, find the one called just **Sequence** (not AsyncSequence or ReactiveSequence) and **drag** it onto the canvas. It becomes the top of your tree. (You can type `Sequence` in the search box above the list to find it.)
say.bit: Drag **Sequence** (the plain one) from Nodes onto the canvas.

target.selector: .palette-item[title^='Ticks children in order until one fails']

say.never: Press **Save** at the top (or **Ctrl+S**). The little dot next to the file name disappears once it's saved. Until you save, nothing is written to the file the robot runs, and a new tree that was never saved is gone if the page reloads.
say.bit: **Save** (Ctrl+S). The dot by the file name goes away.
